rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, Ebu’d- Derdâ, Hasan, Mücâhid, İbrâhim, Katâde ve Süddî
rows.claim: These authorities, as cited by Ebû Bekr-i Râzî, understand the food of the People of the Book as their slaughtered animals.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan, Ebu’d- Derdâ’dan, Hasan ve Mücâhid ve İbrâhim ve Katâde ve Süddî’den rivayet edilmiştir ki

rows.speaker: Ebû Bekr-i Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī says the apparent sense chiefly means slaughter, since bread, oil, and other ordinary foods do not differ by the maker’s religion.
rows.anchor: azher olan bilhassa zebâih murad olunmaktır. Çünkü ekmek, zeytinyağı ve sâir taâmların hükmü imal edenlerin husûsiyetiyle ihtilâf etmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although taʿām can broadly include slaughter and other foods, the special distinction for scripturalists chiefly concerns slaughter and game.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i kitâbı tahsis ederek diğerlerinden ihtiraz eden bu ibâha-i mahsûsanın fâidesi ancak zebâihte zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims agree that an animal dying without proper slaughter is forbidden whoever killed it, whether Muslim, scripturalist, or Magian.
rows.anchor: Muharremâtta zikr olunduğu üzere tezkiyesiz ölenlerin de gerek müslim ve gerek kitâbî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific permission marks religious qualification for slaughter: the slaughterer may be Muslim or from the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: zekât için diyanet yani müslim veya ehl-i kitab olmak şart bulunduğunu anlatmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term taʿām remains general, conditioned on being wholesome: slaughter is expressly permitted, while permissibility of other foods follows by implication.
rows.anchor: zebâihin hıllini dâl bi’l-ibâre, diğerlerinin hıllini dâl bi’lişâre olarak ahz etmek lâzım gelecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may rely on a Jewish or Christian slaughterer’s apparent monotheism without investigating the invocation; direct knowledge that Jesus was invoked makes the meat forbidden.
rows.anchor: bir Yahudî veya Nasrânînin kestiğini acaba ne nâm ile kesti diye tedkike kalkışmayarak ve zâhir-i hâlleriyle iktifâ ederek yemek câizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule also accepts the outward Muslim claim of any Islamic sect, but an apostate’s slaughter is never edible, even if he affiliates with the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: gerek ehl-i sünnet olsun ve gerek olmasın firak-ı İslâmiye’den hepsinin zebîhası helâl olduğunda da şüphe yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Chaste, free Muslim women and chaste, free scripturalist women are lawful for Muslim men to marry with a dowry in marriage, not through open or secret fornication.
rows.anchor: yani hürre ve afîfe Müslüman kadınlar ve kızlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food exchange is reciprocal, but marriage permission runs only one way: Muslim men may marry chaste scripturalist women, while Muslim women may not marry scripturalist men.
rows.anchor: taâm hususunda iki taraftan müsaade gösterilmiş, Müslümanlara hem ehl-i kitâbın taâmlarını yemek hem de ehl-i kitâba Müslüman taâmını it‘âm etmek suretiyle mütekābilen alış veriş helâl kılınmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition in 2:221 on marrying polytheist women is lifted for scripturalist women, while the prior prohibition on giving Muslim women to unbelieving men remains.
rows.anchor: ehl-i kitab kadınları hakkında nesh olunmuş ve mütekābilen Müslüman kadınlarının ehl-i kitâba tezvîcine asla müsaade olunmamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a foundational principle, the rule for human persons and sexual honor is prohibition rather than permissibility.
rows.anchor: nüfûs-ı insâniye ve ırz mesâilinde ibâha değil hurmet asıldır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on marrying polytheist men to believing women reinforces that original rule.
rows.anchor: nehyi ile tekid ve takrir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule is stated still more generally by the declaration that God gives unbelievers no way over believers.
rows.anchor: ile bu hurmet ve nehiy daha umûmî surette tavzih de kılınmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse expressly permits only Muslim men’s marriage to scripturalist women while discussing lawful relations, its silence on the reverse case is a restrictive indication called bayān al-ḍarūra.
rows.anchor: denilen bir kasr vardır. Ve bu suretle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since prohibition is the default in such matters, one must ask whether permission exists, not demand a separate prohibition; the rule has been known by communal consensus since the Prophet’s era.
rows.anchor: asr-ı saadetten beri icmâ‘-ı ümmet ile de mâlum bulunan bu meseleyi ihtârımıza sebep

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlī held that the Arab Christians of Banū Taghlib had adopted little of Christianity beyond drinking wine and so were not Christians for this rule; al-Shāfiʿī chose that view.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali radıyallahu anh Arap Nasârâsından Benî Tağlib hakkında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority and the Hanafi imams permit slaughter by all Arab Christians, judging from the scripture’s apparent wording.
rows.anchor: cumhur ve eimme-i Hanefiyye zâhir-i kitâba nazaran ale’l-umûm Nasârâ-yı Arabın zebîhaları dahi lâ be’se bih demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās limits scripturalist women in the marriage clause to non-belligerents and therefore forbids marrying belligerent Jewish or Christian women.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas nikâh fıkrasında ehl-i kitabdan murad harbî olmayanlar olduğuna ve binâen‘aleyh harbî olan Yehûd ve Nasârâ kadınlarını nikâh câiz olmadığına kāil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: cumhûr-ı ulemâ
rows.claim: The majority holds the verse’s unrestricted wording includes both belligerent and protected scripturalists; marrying a belligerent scripturalist woman is not forbidden, though disliked absent need.
rows.anchor: cumhûr-ı ulemâ âyetin ıtlâkı üzere harbî ve zimmîye şâmil bulunduğuna ve binâen‘aleyh harbî olan ehl-i kitabdan kadın tezevvüc etmek haram değil, bir zarûret bulunmadıkça nihâyet mekruh olduğuna kāildirler.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet commands treating Magians like the People of the Book, except that their women are not to be married and their slaughter is not to be eaten.
rows.anchor: Mecûsîlere ehl-i kitab muamelesi yapınız, fakat kadınlarını nikâh etmemek ve kestiklerini yememek şartıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly permissions concerning scripturalists do not imply their afterlife salvation: whoever rejects the complete Islamic faith and law loses all deeds and is among the hereafter’s losers.
rows.anchor: her kim bu imana, yani bu dîn-i ekmele ve şerî‘at-ı İslâm’a küfr ederse bütün ameli tutulur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must guard against damage to faith and apostasy while eating scripturalist food or marrying their women; marriage to a belligerent woman is disliked.
rows.anchor: onların taâmlarını yerken veya kadınlarını tezevvüc ederken imanı haleldâr etmekten, irtidad tehlikesine düşmekten son derece ihtiraz etmelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage completes discussion of divine covenant law by pairing wholesome food with family life, recalling 4:3, then turns to faithfulness, the afterlife, and purification as the key to worship, under 24:26.
rows.anchor: hayât-ı dünyeviye makāsıdından bulunan tayyibât-ı mâide

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabaʾ means significant or important news.
rows.anchor: “Nebe’”, haber-i mühim demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says some Jews asked the Prophet about his religion; after his answer from 2:136 and hearing Jesus named, they called it the worst religion, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: Îsâ’yı işittikleri zaman “biz sizin dininizden daha şerîr din bilmiyoruz” demişler, bu âyet bunun üzerine nâzil olmuş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reported occasion, the verse may rhetorically answer the Jews’ calling Islam evil by naming their own state as worse; on this view, that points to the religion they disparaged.
rows.anchor: bu sebeb-i nüzûle itiraz etmemekle beraber şu mânayı daha zâhir buluyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers reading the verse as a grave warning to the People of the Book about those God cursed, angered, transformed, and who worshipped Taghut; those people are worse and further astray.
rows.anchor: ve bir de tâgūta tapan tâgūta kulluk eden kimseler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s curse is linked to the Israelites’ breach of covenant in 5:13.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın lânetlediği (فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ م۪يثَاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ [el-Mâide 5/13] bak)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transformed people are identified as the Sabbath people, with their young made apes and their old made swine.
rows.anchor: ashâb-ı sebt olduğu, bunların gençleri maymun, ihtiyarları da hınzır kılığına konulmuş bulunduğu zikrediliyor

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes assign the apes to the Sabbath people and the swine to the companions of Jesus’s table; Elmalılı finds this more fitting because 2:65 mentions only apes for the Sabbath people.
rows.anchor: bazı müfessirîn kırade ashâb-ı sebt, hanâzîr mâide-i Îsâ ashâbıdır demişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maskh can be moral transformation alone, or both outward and moral transformation that produces degradation of life; the latter is called real transformation.
rows.anchor: Mesh-i mânevî; sefâlet-i ahlâkiye intac eden tehavvül, mesh-i sûrî ve mânevî de sefâlet-i ahlâkiye ile beraber sefâlet-i hayâtiyeyi intac eden tehavvüldür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transformed beings do not reproduce; becoming apes and swine means extinction and sterility in total degradation, not evolving into a reproductive animal species.
rows.anchor: Memsuh olanlarda tenasül olmaz, binâen‘aleyh maymun ve hınzır oldular demek, envâ‘-ı hayvânâttan maymun ve hınzır tenasülü yapar bir nevi oldular demek değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who claim humans evolved from apes by generations must also allow the reverse transformation by the same supposed law; this verse answers and warns them.
rows.anchor: insanın da jenerasyon tarîkiyle maymuna inkılab edeceğini bir kanun gibi mülâhaza etmeleri iktizâ eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence from curse to wrath, transformation, and Taghut worship escalates in evil: curse is least, Taghut servitude greatest, and worship of Taghut is the root that entails the rest.
rows.anchor: Âyette lânetten gazaba, gazabdan meshe, meshten ubûdiyyet-i tâgūta doğru giden silsile-i beyan gösteriyor ki bunların hey’et-i mecmû‘ası değil her biri bir şerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ape represents unstable, deceptive imitation without understanding; the swine represents appetite, filth, and abhorrent criminality.
rows.anchor: fakat hakikatte ne yaptığını bilmez, taklid derdiyle her felâkete atılır, sevk edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of Taghut is cross-referenced to the explanation of 2:256 in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: mânası için Sûre-i Bakara’da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the common reading, ʿabada is a perfect verb coordinated with the verbs for cursing and wrath, meaning whoever worshipped Taghut.
rows.anchor: “Abede” fi‘l-i mâzî olarak لَّعَنَهُ veya وَغَضِبَ’ye ma‘tuf olup وَمَنْ عَبَدَ demektir.

rows.speaker: Hamza
rows.claim: Hamza reads the phrase with ḍamma on bāʾ and genitive ṭāʾ as an idāfa construction coordinated with apes and swine; ʿābid is an adjective on the yekuz pattern.
rows.anchor: Hamza kıraatinde bâ’nın zammı ve tâ’nın cerriyle terkîb-i izâfî olarak وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَ okunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They profess belief when they come to the believers, yet enter and leave as unbelievers; their hearts conceal unbelief and corruption, which God knows better than they do.
rows.anchor: mü’min görünürler, hâlbuki kâfir girer kâfir çıkarlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not all of them, but many continually rush into sin, aggression, and illicit gain; lying and abusive speech exemplify aggression, while bribery exemplifies suḥt.
rows.anchor: bunların hepsi değil fakat çoğunu görürsün ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about lying and consuming suḥt in 5:42 is a parallel cross-reference, with bribery as a leading example of illicit gain.
rows.anchor: (سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ اَكَّالُونَ لِلْسُحْتِ [5/42] bak)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rabbāniyyūn and ahbār should forbid sinful speech and illicit eating; rabbāniyyūn are political authorities claiming religious leadership, and ahbār are scholars.
rows.anchor: yani başlarında rabbânîlik iddiasında bulunan evliyâ-yı umûrları siyâsiyyûnu ve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fail to forbid the wrongdoing and at least promote it through silence; their conduct is an ugly political craft that corrupts people’s morals and religion.
rows.anchor: lâekal sükût ile olsun tervic ediyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders and scholars bear the basic responsibility for this corruption, and Taghut is found among them.
rows.anchor: Ve bütün mes’ûliyetin esası bunlardadır. Ve halkın ahlâkını dinini bozan bunlardır. Tâgūt bunlar içindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The political rabbāniyyūn’s responsibility precedes that of the scholars, the ahbār.
rows.anchor: rabbâniyyûnun mes’ûliyeti ahbârdan daha mukaddemdir.

rows.speaker: Ulemâ
rows.claim: Scholars say this is the Qur’an’s strongest and most frightening reprimand of scholars.
rows.anchor: Ulemâ demişlerdir ki Kur’an’da ulemâyı tevbih eden âyetler içinde en şiddetlisi, en korkuncu budur.

rows.speaker: İbn Mübarek
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak’s verse says rulers, bad scholars, and monks are the ones who corrupt religion.
rows.anchor: İbn Mübarek hazretleri de bu âyetin mazmûnunu şu beytiyle ifade etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥurum is the plural of ḥarām and here means a person in ihram whether in the sanctuary or outside it; someone in the sanctuary is covered even without ihram.
rows.anchor: ki muhrim yani gerek Harem’de ve gerek Hil’de olsun ihramda bulunan demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayd can denote edible or inedible game, but custom and the definite article or fullest sense here point to edible game.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A hadith says five creatures may be killed in both the lawful zone and sanctuary: kite, crow, scorpion, mouse, and vicious dog, with snake in one version.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vicious-dog category also indicates that other predatory animals attacking people may be killed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deliberate offender is one who knows he is in ihram and knows hunting is forbidden to him, then intentionally kills game.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The penalty is an equivalent camel, cow, or sheep/goat, with equivalence judged by two trustworthy, upright experts rather than personal estimation.
rows.anchor: katlettiği ava mümâsil en‘âmdan deve, sığır, davardan bir cezâ lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animal penalty must be a sacrificial offering that reaches the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: Kâbe’ye varacak bir hedy olmak üzere lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offender may choose among the livestock offering, feeding the poor, or an equivalent fast.
rows.anchor: veya fukarâ taâmı bir keffâret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Experts assess the game’s value; one buys an offering with it or food for the poor, allotting half a ṣāʿ per poor person, or fasts one day per half ṣāʿ.
rows.anchor: her fakire yarım sâ‘olmak üzere fukarâya verilir. Veyahut her yarım sâ‘yerine bir oruç tutulur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three penalty forms are alternatives, intended to make the offender taste the burden of his deed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s surface might suggest no penalty for accidental or forgetful killing, but the contrary implication is not legally authoritative.

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer, İbn Abbas, Tâvûs, Hasan, İbrâhîm Nehaî ve Zührî
rows.claim: These authorities hold that the penalty also applies to accidental or forgetful killing; Abū Ḥanīfa, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and their companions agree.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer’den, İbn Abbas’tan, Tâvûs’tan, Hasan’dan, İbrâhîm Nehaî’den, Zührî’den rivayete göre hatâ ve nisyanda dahi bu cezâ vardır.

rows.speaker: Hanefiyye ve Mâlikiyye
rows.claim: For Hanafis and Malikis, any game caught or slaughtered by a person in ihram is carrion, not ritually slaughtered; neither that person nor anyone else may eat it.
rows.anchor: Hanefiyye ve Mâlikiyyece meyte hükmündedir, müzekkâ değildir, ne kendisi yiyebilir ne başkası.

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that the game is ritually slaughtered and another person may eat it.
